name: Doodle
tagline: Run group availability polls and convert the selected option into a calendar event

pricing.notes: Typical Pro monthly rate; annual billing can be lower.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Doodle, run group availability polls and convert the selected option into a calendar event. The hard boundary is participant familiarity, calendar connections, reminders, branding, and hosted delivery, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Run group availability polls against one calendar, convert the selected option into a conflict-safe calendar event, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: participant familiarity, calendar connections, reminders, branding, and hosted delivery
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Doodle because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Doodle in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: run group availability polls against one calendar, convert the selected option into a conflict-safe calendar event, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
